title: Franchising Trends for 2013
主要内容: The franchise industry in 2013 is expected to show cautious optimism, with a projected growth rate of 1.4 percent, similar to the previous year. However, franchise leaders are frustrated by the slow pace of growth, attributing it to uncertainties in public policy and the economic recovery. The Affordable Care Act is a major concern, with 31 percent of franchisees planning to cut jobs to stay under the 50-employee threshold. Tax concerns are also significant, with 79 percent of franchisees and 73 percent of franchisors worried about the failure to extend Bush-era tax rates. Access to credit remains a challenge, with over half of franchisees citing a lack of small-business lending as a negative impact. Despite these challenges, modest growth is expected in employment, output, and GDP for franchised businesses. Real estate franchises are expected to perform well due to the recovering housing market, while quick-service restaurants will continue to lead in growth. However, sectors like automotive, retail, and food retail are expected to see less than one percent growth. Franchising trends for 2013 indicate that consumers are becoming more cautious about spending and are trying to extend the life of vehicles and household goods rather than replacing them frequently. The International Franchise Association (IFA) survey highlights that franchisors are more optimistic about the future than franchisees, largely due to the scale of their operations. A franchisor losing one unit typically does not significantly impact its bottom line, whereas a franchisee losing one unit could mean the loss of their entire business. As a result, franchisors are increasingly seeking area developers and master licensees instead of single-unit franchisees. However, even multiunit franchisees are hesitant about expansion, as noted by Aziz Hashim, a multiunit quick-service franchisee, who stated that franchisees are being hit from every angle and will expand at a slower rate in 2013. Despite this, franchised businesses continue to outpace growth in the rest of the private sector, suggesting that franchises will likely continue to lead the way toward economic recovery.
